verdict.rationale: DBOS's architecture is explicitly designed this way: the DBOS library runs embedded in the customer's own application/workers with only Postgres as required infra (dbos-docs-2, dbos-comm-1, dbos-comm-14), while the vendor-hosted Conductor service supplies the orchestration control plane (pause/restart/fork workflows, dashboards, CLI/API) without requiring a separate execution server (dbos-docs-16, dbos-docs-17, dbos-docs-18, dbos-probe-rt-4). Conductor can even be self-hosted if desired (dbos-docs-19), reinforcing that code and data remain in the customer's network by design. Missing for 10: explicit confirmation of exactly what metadata is transmitted to the hosted Conductor control plane, and independent hands-on confirmation that no application data ever leaves the customer's network when using managed Conductor.
